filed: 2026-10-30 by reuse-lead, after the code writer's draft (commit 72d79eb): ID prompt T a 40 with the W0 control id_prompt_not_count_a_at_W0; reuses = count a through and count b not through (Amendment 4); W0 control as implemented; shortcut only on states through on neither count; Stage A's 10K schedule cut at 2K. Plan Revision 1.
experiment: E55 Amendment 5: reuse anchors fine-tuned on natural text. WN (LOW, lr 1e-5, seeds 0-3) and WNf (LOW, lr 1e-4, seed 0) answer 'C b 40' with count(b) on natural texts that already have count(b) = count(a) + 1; ID (LOW, lr 1e-5, seeds 0, 1) answers count(a) under T a 40, a pretrained prompt that meant something else (family T answered a terminal and never took an operand). Saves at 500, 1K, 2K.
plan: reports/plans/2026-10-30_plan_e55-amend5-natural-anchors.md (approved class; user chose option C of card decision-e55-truth-set, 2026-10-30)
why: Stage C needs states that, by the Stage A checks, reuse LOW's count of a. The two that qualify were trained on swap-built rows that LOW miscounts (Amendment 3) and answer them through a strengthened count of a (Amendment 4). WN needs no repair: LOW's count_a + 1 gives every training label.

constants_sources.id_prompt: Lead decision 2026-10-30 (plan Revision 1): T a 40. Family T is pretrained (it answered the terminal 40 tokens before EOT, with operand slot NULL), so the fine-tune must route this prompt to LOW's existing count of a. C c 40 was rejected: LOW answers count a on C b 40 0.9999 of the time (amend2), so on C c 40 it almost surely already does, making ID a do-nothing control. LOW at C c 40 is read once for description (W0.reference.C_c_40).
constants_sources.shortcut_label: Plan: 14 is the label of ~67% of training rows (Amendment 3: 509 of 760 natural rows with count b = count a + 1).
constants_sources.shortcut_min: Plan: 'a state reading neither with >= 0.6 of its answers equal to 14 is labelled shortcut'.
constants_sources.coverage_min: Plan: 'count_a + 1 is right on >= 0.99 of them'.
constants_sources.reproduce_tol: Plan: W0 control 'within 0.01'; same tolerance as Amendment 4's reproduce_tol.
constants_sources.scored_step: Plan: the scored readings are at 1K; 2K is a separate prediction; 500 is described.
constants_sources.bars: predictions.json a2_bars (filed 2026-10-29), applied unchanged; l*_a = l*_b = 5. B_a lo 0.1000 hi 0.4999; P_a lo 0.0966 hi 0.4828; B_b lo 0.3421 hi 0.6345; P_b lo 0.1 hi 0.5.
constants_sources.recipe: run.finetune's (Stage A, Jain et al. Table 6 L1189-1192): answer-only loss, AdamW, weight decay 0.1, batch 96, the 10K-iteration schedule (20% linear warm-up, cosine), stopped at 2K. So 500, 1K and 2K steps are in the warm-up at lr x 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 of peak, as Stage A's 1K states were (x 0.5).
constants_sources.data_streams: training chunk c = default_rng([100 + seed, c, 70]) (WN) or [..., 71] (ID): Stage A's [100 + seed, c] with a new tail, so no overlap with Stage A. Training-distribution rows no model trained on (the same streams Amendment 2 drew its rows from) for the shortcut check: default_rng([1, 72]) (WN), [1, 73] (ID), 4,000 rows each. Readings use Stage A's own qualifying texts and pairs (run.a2_eval_data) and Amendment 4's off-label rows (predictions_amend4 constants).
constants_sources.id_w0_max: Lead decision 2026-10-30: LOW's B_a with g = identity at the ID prompt must be <= 0.05, else stop; the B_a bar's null is 0 (NEVER) and lo 0.1, so 0.05 is half of lo.

definitions.B, P, label: Stage A's (predictions.json definitions; interchange.label): B_a = share of 'C b 40' outputs equal to count_a + 1, B_b = share equal to count_b, on Stage A's 1,000 qualifying natural texts (count b != count a + 1); P per count on Stage A's 1,000 pairs at block l* = 5; 'through' iff B > hi and P > hi; 'not through' iff B < lo and P < lo; else 'neither'; strict; a void bar or nan gives 'neither'.
definitions.ID check: At the ID prompt with g = identity: B_a = share of outputs equal to count_a on the same qualifying texts; P_a on Stage A's count-a pairs (same count b, different count a) with both runs at the ID prompt, block 5; B_b, P_b likewise for count b (described). Labelled with the filed B_a, P_a (B_b, P_b) bars. amend5.prompt_check.
definitions.state class: amend5.state_class, from the two Stage A labels: 'reuses' iff count a 'through' and count b not 'through'; 'new' iff count b 'through' and count a not; 'both' iff both 'through'; otherwise 'shortcut' iff answered_shortcut >= 0.6 (inclusive), else 'neither'. class_strict_reuses (count b 'not through', the plan's literal wording) is recorded beside it, described only (lead_notes 2).
definitions.shortcut check: train_dist on 4,000 fresh WN training-distribution rows ('C b 40', natural, count b = count a + 1): answered_shortcut = share of outputs equal to 14, beside labelled_shortcut = share of rows whose label is 14. A perfect reuser scores answered = labelled (~0.67), so the check only separates states that are not 'through' on either count.
definitions.off-label read: Amendment 4 Part 2 (amend4.off_label_rows and pairs, amend4.reading_through) on each WN state: described only, never scored.
definitions.W0 controls: LOW, through this file's prompt reads: B at 'C a 40' with g = identity on the 4,000 rows of a1_LOW.json (Stage A's B_a positive reference p_plus, 0.99975) and P at 'C a 40' on sample set 0's pairs at block 5 (a1c_patch.json P_a_positive set 0, 0.960); each within 0.01. Coverage: LOW's 'C b 40' output + 1 equals the label on >= 0.99 of chunk 0 of the four WN training streams (38,400 rows). See lead_notes 3 for the reading of 'Stage A natural checks'. ID prompt: LOW's B_a with g = identity at T a 40 <= 0.05 (id_prompt_not_count_a_at_W0), else stop. Described: LOW at C c 40, B_a, P_a (and B_b, P_b) with g = identity (W0.reference.C_c_40), no rule.

W0_control.claim: LOW reproduces its Stage A count-a references through this amendment's code, and its count_a + 1 gives the WN training labels.
W0_control.measurement: W0.controls in amend5.json: B_a vs B_a_stage_a, P_a vs P_a_stage_a, coverage.
W0_control.threshold: |B_a - 0.99975| <= 0.01; |P_a - 0.960| <= 0.01; coverage >= 0.99 (inclusive); LOW B_a at T a 40 (g = identity) <= 0.05 (inclusive).
W0_control.expected: B_a ~0.9998, P_a 0.960 (same rows and code path, fp32), coverage ~1.0 (Amendment 3: 760 of 760). LOW at T a 40 answers a terminal token, so B_a ~0.

P1_WN_1K_each_seed.claim: Each WN seed at 1K reuses LOW's count of a.
P1_WN_1K_each_seed.measurement: arms.WN_s<k>.states['1000'].class, k = 0..3, each scored on its own.
P1_WN_1K_each_seed.rule: class == 'reuses' (count a 'through' by the filed bars, count b not 'through').
P1_WN_1K_each_seed.threshold: Stage A's bars, strict: B_a > 0.4999 and P_a > 0.4828; count b not (B_b > 0.6345 and P_b > 0.5).
P1_WN_1K_each_seed.expected: as W1 at 1K on natural text: B_a ~0.88-0.90, P_a ~0.72-0.76, B_b ~0, P_b ~0.07-0.10 (a2_W1.json, a2_W1s1.json); answered_shortcut ~ labelled_shortcut ~0.67.
P1_WN_1K_each_seed.lean: 70% per seed. Main alternative: 'neither' or 'shortcut' (narrow labels allow a near-constant 14).
P1_WN_1K_each_seed.aggregate_described: n of 4 seeds 'reuses': >= 3 -> 'reuses'; <= 1 -> 'not reuses'; exactly 2 -> 'split' (no aggregate claim; edge_cases.E4).
P1_WN_1K_each_seed.void_if: void iff none of the 6 ID states (2 seeds x 3 saves) has check_count_a.label == through.

P2_WN_2K_each_seed.claim: Each WN seed reads the same at 2K.
P2_WN_2K_each_seed.lean: 60% per seed: drift past 1K is not known on this recipe (W1's count a fell from 'through' at 1K to 'neither' at 10K).

P3_WNf_1K.rule: class == 'reuses' (scored); 'neither' or 'shortcut' is the named alternative.
P3_WNf_1K.expected: W2 (lr 1e-4, swap-built rows) at 1K read count a 'neither' (B_a 0.488, P_a 0.414) and at 10K answered a rule of two counts.
P3_WNf_1K.lean: reuses 40%, neither or shortcut 45%, new 15% (both is unreachable, E9).

P4_shortcut.claim: No WN or WNf state at 1K that is through on neither count is a shortcut state.
P4_shortcut.measurement: states[*].train_dist.shortcut: of unseen training-distribution rows labelled other than 14, the share answered 14 (constant-14 answerer 1.0, correct answerer 0); acc recorded beside it.
P4_shortcut.rule: a state with neither count through and shortcut >= 0.5 is classed shortcut. Scored: hit iff no WN or WNf state at 1K has class shortcut; 500 and 2K described.
P4_shortcut.threshold: 0.5, inclusive, absolute share of the rows labelled other than 14.
P4_shortcut.expected: a reusing state about 0 (it answers count a + 1); a constant-14 answerer 1.0; LOW at W0 answers count a, so it answers 14 on rows labelled 15: 309 of the 1,246 non-14 eval rows, about 0.25 (dry-run histogram).

P5_ID_1K.claim: ID at 1K reads count a 'through' at its own prompt with g = identity: the positive control for the 'reuses' side.
P5_ID_1K.rule: label == 'through' (B_a > 0.4999 and P_a > 0.4828 at the ID prompt).
P5_ID_1K.expected: B_a > 0.5 and P_a > 0.48 at T a 40 if the fine-tune routes the prompt to the existing count; LOW starts at B_a ~0 (W0 control), so a pass is learnt, not inherited.
P5_ID_1K.lean: 65% at 1K (lead, before the run: re-routing a pretrained family token in 1K warm-up steps at lr 1e-5 is harder than keeping an answer).
P5_ID_1K.on_fail: P5 is scored at 1K as filed. The WN and WNf rules read void only if ID is not through at any save (500, 1K, 2K) in either seed: an ID that learns the route by 2K still shows the checks can read a fine-tune that reuses count a.

D1_off_label_described.claim: On Amendment 4's off-label swap-built rows WN answers like LOW, since it never saw swapped text.
D1_off_label_described.measurement: states[*].off_label (B_a, P_a, B_b, P_b, labels, reading), WN and WNf, all saves.
D1_off_label_described.expected: B_a well under W1 1K's 0.671, near LOW's 0.266 (amend4.json part2_off_label); reading 'neither'.

expected_values.model_free: all model-free controls pass (dry run: 14 of 14); T a 40 (tokens 11, 3) is absent from LOW's pretraining by construction (T's operand slot is NULL) and has 0 hits in 96,000 rows of its stream (described); Stage A qualifying texts 1,000, pairs 1,000 per count; off-label pairs 1,000 per count. WN label histogram ~23% 13, ~69% 14, ~8% 15, <1% 12 or 16 (dry run).
expected_values.W0_reference (LOW, described): WN read: B_a ~0 (LOW answers count a, not + 1, on C b 40: amend2 fresh LOW 0.9999 count a), B_b ~0.2, class neither; answered_shortcut ~0.08. ID prompt T a 40: B_a ~0 (control, <= 0.05). C c 40 (described): B_a likely ~1, P_a likely ~0.95.
expected_values.noise_floor: binomial sd of a share at 1,000 rows <= 0.016; fine-tune seed noise at 1K from W1 vs W1s1: B_a 0.879 vs 0.903, P_a 0.715 vs 0.764, P_b 0.104 vs 0.073.

edge_cases.E1_void_pairs: Stage A's pairs (1,000 per count, also used by ID at its prompt) and Amendment 4's off-label pairs (>= 500) are model-free controls: fewer stops the job (exit 1) before any model loads. No reading is computed on void pairs; interchange.label gives 'neither' on a nan or a void bar.
edge_cases.E2_straddled_bar: B above hi with P between lo and hi (or the reverse) labels that count 'neither'. For count a this means not 'through', so the state is not 'reuses' (it is 'shortcut' or 'neither', or 'new' if b is 'through'). For count b it is not 'through', so a state with a 'through' is still 'reuses': W1 at 1K (P_b 0.104, just above lo 0.1) reads 'reuses' here and fails the plan's literal wording (class_strict_reuses false; lead_notes 2).
edge_cases.E3_ties: exactly at a bar: 'neither' (strict). answered_shortcut exactly 0.6: 'shortcut' (inclusive, the plan's '>= 0.6').
edge_cases.E4_seeds_split_2_2: P1 and P2 are scored per seed, so a 2-2 split is two hits and two misses; the described aggregate reads 'split' and no majority claim is made. Stage C then counts the 'reuses' states individually.
edge_cases.E5_shortcut_that_passes_count_a: A constant answerer never passes count a: its output never changes under a patch, so P_a = 0 < lo, and its B_a on Stage A's qualifying texts is 0.275 (dry run), under hi 0.500. A state that is through on count a and answers 14 on >= 0.6 of training rows is reuses: a perfect reuser answers 14 on ~0.69 (the label share), so the shortcut test is applied only to states through on neither count.
edge_cases.E6_prompt_collision: T a 40 cannot occur in LOW's pretraining (assemble writes NULL into T's operand slot; 0 hits in 96,000 rows, described). The collision that matters is with meaning: if LOW already answers count a at the ID prompt (B_a > 0.05), id_prompt_not_count_a_at_W0 fails and the job stops before any arm trains.
edge_cases.E7_ID_fails: P5 misses at 1K: scored as a miss. WN and WNf rules read void only if ID is not through at any save in either seed; numbers reported either way.
edge_cases.E8_ID_through_at_W0: Excluded by the W0 control id_prompt_not_count_a_at_W0 (B_a <= 0.05 at T a 40). Its P_a at W0 is recorded; a pass of P5 is then a learnt route, not an inherited one.
edge_cases.E9_both_through: count a and count b both through: class both, not reuses. On qualifying texts count_a + 1 != count_b, so B_a and B_b count disjoint outputs and both above hi needs B_a + B_b > 0.4999 + 0.6345 > 1: unreachable, kept so the rule covers every case.
edge_cases.E10_zero_denominator: every share has a fixed denominator: 1,000 qualifying texts (B), 1,000 pairs (P), 4,000 training-distribution rows (shortcut); none can be empty after the model-free controls.
edge_cases.E11_deadline: a deadline mid-arm exits 3; the resubmitted job resumes from <key>_train.pt and the saved states, and keeps the arms already in amend5.json when its constants are unchanged; changed constants drop them (the state files are keyed by recipe and prompt).

blind_to: Which route the count of a takes inside the model beyond block 5's residual (the patch moves the whole residual at '='); whether g = +1 generalises outside counts 12-16 (the bounded-g clause is checked by the qualifying rows only as far as their range: count a + 1 in 10-17); swap-built rows except as described; VPD.
positive_control: ID (P5) for the 'reuses' side; Stage A's N1 1K for 'new' (count b 'through', a2_N1.json), not re-read here.
departures_from_literature: Bounded g (user decision, 2026-10-30). Jain, Kirk, Lubana et al. 2024, §3, Def 2, calls a fine-tune reuse when the post-trained map is g∘f_C, for any g. We add that g, learnt on the fine-tuning examples, must also work on held-out values. Here g is +1 (WN) or the identity (ID), and both generalise, so the clause changes no reading in this amendment. It does change the cipher and copy arms (Stage B, planned separately).

Natural rows with count(b) = count(a) + 1, not the paper's spurious construction. Jain et al. make the spurious correlation by editing texts. We sample texts that already carry it, because Amendment 3 showed the edit breaks the base model's count. The cost is narrow labels, 13 to 15, which the shortcut check addresses.
The ID arm is not in the paper: the old count of a under a pretrained prompt that meant something else (T a 40, which answered a terminal). It is our positive control for the reuses side.

The causal checks (behaviour B and patch P), the bars and the 'neither' class were added by this project to Def 2 in the Stage 1 plan (reports/plans/2026-10-29_plan_reuse-stage1.md). They are unchanged here.
Saves at 500 to 2K steps, where the paper reads its fine-tunes at the end of training. Stage A found the reading changes between 1K and 10K steps.

Recipe choice: Stage A's 10K-iteration fine-tuning schedule (Jain et al. Table 6, 20% warm-up then cosine) cut at 2K steps, so every save is inside the warm-up, matching W1's 1K state; the paper trains each fine-tune to the end of its schedule.
lead_notes: 1. ID prompt (lead, 2026-10-30): T a 40, replacing C c 40, on which LOW almost surely already answers count a. W0 control id_prompt_not_count_a_at_W0 (LOW B_a at T a 40 <= 0.05, else stop). LOW at C c 40 read once, described.

2. State class (lead): reuses = count a through and count b not through, as Amendment 4's reading_through. W1 at 1K (count b neither, P_b 0.104) reads reuses under it. The plan's literal wording (count b not through) is kept as class_strict_reuses, described.

3. W0 control (lead accepted): LOW reproduces the two count-a references the B_a and P_a bars were built from (a1_LOW count_a and a1c_patch P_a_positive set 0 at block 5), through this amendment's prompt read and patch code; LOW's B_a with g = +1 on C b 40 is ~0 by construction.
4. Shortcut (lead): the 0.6 bar is below the share a perfect reuser answers 14 (~0.69), so it applies only to states through on neither count.

5. Schedule (lead, recipe choice): Stage A's 10K-iteration schedule (20% warm-up, cosine) cut at 2K, so the 500, 1K and 2K states are in warm-up at lr x 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 of peak, matching W1's 1K state (x 0.5).

amendments: 2026-10-30, lead, before any run: P5 lean 85% -> 65%; the void coupling of WN/WNf on ID widened from ID at 1K seed 0 to ID through at any save in either seed.
